cve_summary: GDAL through 3.0.1 has a poolDestroy double free in OGRExpatRealloc in ogr/ogr_expat.cpp when the 10MB threshold is exceeded.

judge_vs_vulnerable.rationale: In OGRExpatUnknownEncodingHandler, the reference implementation explicitly sets info->data, info->convert, and info->release to nullptr after filling the map, while the candidate never touches these fields. Since expat allocates the XML_Encoding struct on the stack and does not zero-initialize it before invoking the user handler, the candidate leaves convert/release as uninitialized stack garbage; expat later invokes these as function pointers (e.g. on encoding release), so a crafted XML document declaring an unrecognized encoding whose name happens to match 'WINDOWS-1252'/'ISO-8859-15' (attacker-controlled input) can trigger a call through an uninitialized function pointer, a serious memory-safety/code-execution risk. Additionally the candidate uses case-sensitive strcmp instead of the case-insensitive EQUAL comparison used by the reference, and OGRExpatRealloc omits freeing ptr on allocation-size rejection (memory leak) - both secondary but real behavioral differences.

judge_vs_fixed.rationale: The reference_implementation only contains OGRExpatRealloc and is missing FillWINDOWS1252, FillISO885915, OGRExpatUnknownEncodingHandler, and OGRCreateExpatXMLParser, all of which are explicitly required by the specification. Since the bulk of the specified behavior is absent from the reference, there is no basis to judge behavioral equivalence for most of the spec, making this comparison degenerate rather than a meaningful equivalence check.
